dedupe_keys.name: usace generic depth damage relationships for residential structures economic guidance memoranda 01 03 and 04 01

description: Economic Guidance Memorandum 04-01 of 10 October 2003 releases generic depth-damage curves for U.S. Army Corps of Engineers flood damage reduction studies, covering one-storey, two-or-more-storey and split-level homes with basements; its first enclosure repeats the curves for the same homes without basements, published in 2000. The Flood Damage Data Collection Program built the curves from losses recorded in major U.S. floods from 1996 to 2001. Regression found quadratic and cubic forms with depth as the only variable most efficient, and content damage is expressed as a percentage of structure value, so no content-to-structure survey is needed. Coverage: U.S. single-family residential structures, for structure and content damage. Access: free PDF memoranda with the curve tables. Licence: U.S. government work. Caveats: cleanup costs, unpaid labour and emergency actions are excluded, the memo explains how to enter the curves in HEC-FDA and warns against mixing them with separately entered content values, and the underlying data are over twenty years old. Simulation uses: stage-damage inputs to flood damage and benefit-cost models, including HEC-FDA and structure-level loss estimates. Related records: the JRC global depth-damage functions, the USACE National Structure Inventory and the FEMA NFIP claims.
